# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction enrichment logic.

import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions


def mk(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ["remark"]:
        if col not in df:
            df[col] = ""
    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df:
        df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 1000.0
    if "transactionDate" not in df:
        df["transactionDate"] = "01/01/2022"
    return df


print("=== 1. HDFC credit whose remark is a long all-numeric string -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT ===")
df = mk([{"description": "ACME TRADERS CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0, "type": "CREDIT",
          "remark": "0000000000012345"}])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING")
print(out[["description", "remark", "transactionCategory"]].to_string())

print("\n=== 2. HDFC salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code -> SALARY ===")

out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING")
print(out[["description", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory"]].to_string())

print("\n=== 5. HDFC offsetting credit right after matching debit -> REVERSAL ===")
df = mk([{"description": "IMPS TXN 1234 JOHN DOE", "amount": 2500.0, "type": "DEBIT"},
         {"description": "IMPS TXN 1234 JOHN DOE", "amount": 2500.0, "type": "CREDIT"}])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING")
print(out[["description", "type", "transactionCategory"]].to_string())

print("\n=== 3. ICICI transfer narration with leading direction word -> payee name ===")

out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df, "SAVING")
print(out[["description", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]].to_string())

steps.message:
All five reported behaviours are fixed with five single-token corrections. Each was an off-by-one boundary/offset or a literal mismatch inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the maintainer predicted.

## Fixes

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`** — cheque deposit on all-numeric reference
`remark.str.len().eq(15)` was paired with `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (11 zeros + 5 digits = 16 chars), so the rule was unreachable dead code and every such credit fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. Changed to `.eq(16)`. The sibling rule at `HDFC.py:215` also keys off `^[0-9]{16}$`, confirming the 16-char remark form.

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`** — salary sub-tag on bare numeric narration
Guard read `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the whole codebase (Controller dispatch, `Purpose.py`, `ICICI.py:105`) uses `"SAVING"`, so this never fired. Changed to `"SAVING"`.

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`** — reversal vs bounce on an offsetting credit
Compared the credit's narration against `description.shift(periods=2)` while the type/amount checks used `shift(periods=1)`, so an adjacent debit/credit pair skipped the `REVERSAL` rule and fell to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule on the next line. Changed to `shift(periods=1)`, matching `ICICI.py:49`, `Saraswat.py:20`, `StandardCharted.py:60`.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`** — payee on 4-field slash bill transfer
`BIL/INFT/<ref>/<name>` (`count("/")==3`) used `sep_by_(2,3)`, lifting the numeric reference; the downstream scrub at `ICICI.py:233` then blanked it for containing 6+ digits. Changed to `sep_by_(3,4)` (final field), consistent with the 5-field variant on line 148.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`** — counterparty on leading-direction-word narration
`py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0, i.e. the direction word itself (`"To"` was then wiped to empty by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` scrub, `"From"` survived as a wrong name). Changed to `index=1`, matching `DCB.py:80-81` and `Kotak.py:233` which use `index=1` for the same two-group shape.

## Verification

- Each of the five rows now labels correctly (`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `SALARY`, `REVERSAL`, `John Doe`, `John Doe`), confirmed both through the bank scripts and end-to-end via the `/categorizeTransaction` endpoint.
- Diffed old vs. new output over a 4,944-row synthetic corpus (32 HDFC × 7 remark forms and 26 ICICI narration shapes × both account types × 4 amounts × both directions). Every changed row belongs to one of the four fixed rule families; nothing else moved — notably the 5-field `BIL/INFT/.../Payment/ACME LTD` form and all `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rows are untouched.
- Ordered-sequence tests confirm the reversal rule fires only for an adjacent matching debit→credit pair, still yields `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` for non-rail narrations, and no longer spuriously matches a row two positions back.

One unrelated pre-existing issue surfaced during endpoint testing: `salary_detection` only drops its temporary `dateSal` (Period dtype) column inside the `salaryDetect == True` branch, so when no salary is found `to_json` raises `OverflowError` on this environment's pandas. It reproduces identically on unmodified code and is outside the scope of these reports, so I left it alone — flagging it in case you want it addressed separately.
